questions.solution:

__
 
• The reason to use **"does" **in the blank is to form a grammatically correct question in the present simple tense.
 
• In English, when forming questions in the present simple tense, we use the auxiliary verb **"do" (or "does" for the third person singular) **to help construct the question.
 
• This structure helps create a grammatically correct and interrogative sentence.
 
• Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence**: *"What **does**__ your dad do at the Ministry of Magic, anyway?”*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• **Have: **In interrogative sentences, the auxiliary verb** "have"** is often used to form questions in the present perfect or past perfect tenses.
 
• **Do: ****"Do" **is used with the base form of the main verb for questions in the present simple tense
 
• **Is: **The auxiliary verb **"is" **is used in interrogative sentences when forming questions in the present simple tense for singular subjects, specifically when the subject is a third-person singular pronoun (he, she, it) or a singular noun.
